title: Finite-horizon success probability bound
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $N$ has total nonhalting probability at most $T(|x|)$ on every input $x$, and every halted run outputs the one-symbol indicator of whether $x\in L$. For any input $x$ and any positive integer $t$, every choice word whose run halts produces that correct output, and a uniformly chosen Boolean choice word of length $t$ produces a halted run with that output with probability at least $1-T(|x|)/t$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$N$ satisfies the stated nonhalting-probability bound with $T$
Every halted run outputs the one-symbol indicator of membership in $L$
